entities.summary: Eystein Orre was a Norwegian noble who played a pivotal role in the late 11th-century Viking Age, specifically during the reign of King Harald Hardrada, who sought to reclaim the English throne. In 1066, Eystein Orre fought at the Battle of Stamford Bridge, alongside other Norwegian warriors, against the invading forces of King Harold II of England, resulting in a crushing defeat for the English. The Battle of Stamford Bridge marked a turning point in the Viking Age, as it halted the English invasion and led to the eventual defeat of King Harald Hardrada at the Battle of Hastings. This event had a lasting impact on the medieval Scandinavian kingdoms, leading to a period of increased cooperation and cultural exchange between Norway, Denmark, and Sweden. The legacy of Eystein Orre can be seen in the rich cultural heritage of Norway, which continues to celebrate its Viking heritage through festivals, literature, and art.
